If $f(p^m) = g(m)$ for every prime $p$ and every $m \ge 1$, then $f$ is the multiplicative function with prime-power values $g$, that is, the arithmetic function $n \mapsto \prod_{q \mid n} g(v_q(n))$ for $n \ge 1$, where $q$ runs over the primes dividing $n$ and $v_q(n)$ is…
nodes.title: A multiplicative function with prescribed prime-power values

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers. If $d$ is a unitary divisor of $mn$, then $\gcd(d, m)$ is a unitary divisor of $m$.
nodes.title: Gcd with a coprime factor preserves unitary divisors

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero and $c \in R$. Let $c^{\Omega}$ be the arithmetic function $n \mapsto c^{\Omega(n)}$ for $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. Then $c^{\Omega}$ is completely multiplicative: for all natural numbers $m$ and $n$, its value at $mn$ is the product of its values at $m$ and at $n$.
nodes.title: Complete multiplicativity of $c^{\Omega}$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative monoid with zero and $g : \mathbb{N} \to R$. The arithmetic function $n \mapsto \prod_{q \mid n} g(v_q(n))$ for $n \ge 1$, where $q$ runs over the primes dividing $n$ and $v_q(n)$ is the exponent of $q$ in $n$, is multiplicative.
nodes.title: Multiplicativity of the function with prescribed prime-power values

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero and $c \in R$. The arithmetic function $n \mapsto c^{\Omega(n)}$ for $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity, is multiplicative.
nodes.title: Multiplicativity of $c^{\Omega}$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring. If $f$ and $g$ are multiplicative arithmetic functions with values in $R$, then their unitary convolution $f \sqcup g$, given by $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d} f(d)\, g(n/d)$ with $d$ running over the unitary divisors of $n$, is multiplicative.
nodes.title: The unitary convolution of multiplicative functions is multiplicative

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers. If $a$ is a unitary divisor of $m$ and $b$ is a unitary divisor of $n$, then $ab$ is a unitary divisor of $mn$.
nodes.title: Products of unitary divisors of coprime numbers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative monoid with zero, let $g : \mathbb{N} \to R$, and let $n \ne 0$ be a natural number. The multiplicative function with value $g(m)$ at every prime power $p^m$ with $m \ge 1$ takes the value $\prod_{q \mid n} g(v_q(n))$ at $n$, where $q$ runs over the primes dividing $n$ and $v_q(n)$ is the exponent of $q$ in the factorization of $n$.
nodes.title: Value of the function with prescribed prime-power values

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative monoid with zero and $g : \mathbb{N} \to R$. The multiplicative function with prime-power values $g$, given by $n \mapsto \prod_{q \mid n} g(v_q(n))$ for $n \ge 1$ (with $q$ running over the primes dividing $n$ and $v_q(n)$ the exponent of $q$ in $n$), takes the value $1$ at $n = 1$, whatever $g(0)$ is.
nodes.title: The function with prescribed prime-power values is $1$ at $1$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative monoid with zero and $g : \mathbb{N} \to R$. For every prime $p$ and every $m \ge 1$, the multiplicative function with prime-power values $g$, given by $n \mapsto \prod_{q \mid n} g(v_q(n))$ for $n \ge 1$ (with $q$ running over the primes dividing $n$ and $v_q(n)$ the exponent of $q$ in $n$), takes the value $g(m)$ at $p^m$.
nodes.title: The function with prescribed prime-power values at a prime power

This is the arithmetic function $f$ with values in $R$ given by $f(0) = 0$ and $f(n) = \prod_{p \mid n} g(v_p(n))$ for $n \ge 1$, where the product runs over the primes $p$ dividing $n$ and $v_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. It is multiplicative, it takes the value $g(m)$ at every prime power $p^m$ with $m \ge 1$, and its value at $1$ is…
nodes.title: Multiplicative function with prescribed values at prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero, let $c \in R$, and let $c^{\Omega}$ be the arithmetic function with values in $R$ that is $0$ at $0$ and $c^{\Omega(n)}$ at each $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. For every natural number $n \ne 0$, its value at $n$ is $c^{\Omega(n)}$.
nodes.title: Value of $c^{\Omega}$ at a positive integer

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero, let $c \in R$, and let $c^{\Omega}$ be the arithmetic function with values in $R$ that is $0$ at $0$ and $c^{\Omega(n)}$ at each $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. Its value at $1$ is $1$.
nodes.title: Value of $c^{\Omega}$ at $1$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero, let $c \in R$, and let $c^{\Omega}$ be the arithmetic function with values in $R$ that is $0$ at $0$ and $c^{\Omega(n)}$ at each $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. For every prime $p$ and every natural number $m$, its value at $p^m$ is $c^m$.
nodes.title: Value of $c^{\Omega}$ at prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a monoid with zero and let $c \in R$. This is the arithmetic function $c^{\Omega}$ with values in $R$ given by $c^{\Omega}(0) = 0$ and $c^{\Omega}(n) = c^{\Omega(n)}$ for $n \ge 1$, where $\Omega(n)$ is the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. It is completely multiplicative.
nodes.title: The arithmetic function $c^{\Omega}$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $f$ and $g$ be arithmetic functions with values in $R$. For every natural number $n$, their unitary convolution $f \sqcup g$ satisfies $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$, where the sum runs over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$: for $n \ge 1$ these are the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd(d, n/d) = 1$, and for $n = 0$ there are none, so the sum is $0$.
nodes.title: Unitary convolution as a sum over unitary divisors

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $f$ and $g$ be arithmetic functions with values in $R$. Their unitary convolution $f \sqcup g$, defined by $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$ over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$, satisfies $(f \sqcup g)(1) = f(1)\, g(1)$.
nodes.title: Unitary convolution at $1$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $f$ and $g$ be arithmetic functions with values in $R$. For every prime $p$ and every natural number $m \ge 1$, their unitary convolution $f \sqcup g$ satisfies $(f \sqcup g)(p^m) = f(1)\, g(p^m) + f(p^m)\, g(1)$.
nodes.title: Unitary convolution at prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring. The unitary convolution of two arithmetic functions $f$ and $g$ with values in $R$ is the arithmetic function $f \sqcup g$ given by $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$, where the sum runs over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$: for $n \ge 1$ these are the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd(d, n/d) = 1$, and $0$ has no unitary divisors. In particular $(f \sqcup g)(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Unitary convolution

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every natural number $m$, the unitary divisors of $p^m$, that is, the divisors $d$ of $p^m$ with $\gcd(d, p^m/d) = 1$, are exactly $1$ and $p^m$.
nodes.title: Unitary divisors of a prime power
